findings.title: Same-frame ESC + popover/QoS click: on_ui_press runs at MAP time on the pre-cancel selection — demolish/lane commands the old handle_input never produced
findings.location: app/input/mouse.odin:119,185 (phase-1 Cancel queued, then on_ui_press called synchronously) + app/main.odin:751-773 popover_click + app/qos_panel.odin:211-213
findings.evidence: OLD (a4d6e9e app/main.odin:536-541 then 578-592): the ESC block cleared sel_pipe/sel_node BEFORE the press block, so popover_click/qos_panel_click saw sel<0 and returned false (no demolish, click fell through). NEW: mouse_map only QUEUES Intent(Cancel{}) at map time; the press branch then calls inp.on_ui_press(...) synchronously with the selection STILL SET — popover_click's demolish button executes inp.demolish_node/pipe on the stale selection; qos_panel_click's row click cycles lanes on the stale pipe.
findings.detail: Same-frame ESC + click on the demolish popover button (or a QoS row): old code deselected first → hook missed → no command. New code demolishes/lane-cycles → a Command the old code never emitted on that frame. Mouse-path command-stream parity broken — the round's ONE hard blocker category.
findings.recommended_fix: Mirror the deselect into map-time state like placing_eff (e.g. sel_eff cleared when esc_cancelled, with the hooks evaluated against it), or execute the frame's phase-1 intents before mapping the press branch. Add a pinning scenario once the harness wires on_ui_press stubs.

findings.title: Same-frame ESC + left-release while placing: the placement ghost's drag.active routes the release into Drag_Release, which click-selects WITHOUT re-checking the Cancel-set swallow latch
findings.location: app/input/mouse.odin:233-246 (release chain branches on pre-execution drag.active) + app/input/exec.odin:105-114 (Cursor_Move ghost sets drag.active while placing), 124-133 (Drag_Release has no press_swallowed check; Select at 138-145 has it)
findings.evidence: While placing, every move frame sets inp.drag.active=true (exec.odin Cursor_Move placing branch; poll_mouse emits a Mouse_Move every frame). On an [ESC + release@S] frame (press anchored at S earlier): placing_eff=-1 + drag.active=true → the DRAG branch emits Cursor_Move+Drag_Release. Executor: Cancel clears drag + sets press_swallowed=true, Cursor_Move no-ops, then Drag_Release: commit_draw no-ops (drag_to=0), moved=0 (release==press), release_ui_hit false → click_select(S) fires — the latch is never consulted. OLD (a4d6e9e:531-534 then 640/746): the cancel block cleared drag.active + latched the swallow FIRST; the release chain then fell to the plain-release branch gated on !press_swallowed → total no-op.
findings.detail: Old: ESC+release while placing = no-op. New: the release click-selects whatever sits at the press point — a selection delta (and selection drives the popover/QoS/phase-2 targets). Mouse-path parity broken.
findings.recommended_fix: Re-check press_swallowed inside the Drag_Release executor before click_select (mirroring Select), and/or branch the release chain on a drag_eff that treats a same-frame Cancel as drag-cleared (drag_eff := inp.drag.active && !esc_cancelled). Pin with an [ESC + non-moved release] scenario.

findings.title: Right+left chord: Press_Anchor emitted AFTER Right_Click undoes right_click_select's was_dragging swallow latch
findings.evidence: Chord path emits [Right_Click, Press_Anchor]; right_click_select sets press_swallowed=true when it interrupts a drag, then Press_Anchor clears it. The fix's own comment justifies Press_Anchor only for the same-frame Cancel case.
findings.detail: Reachable only via a mixed-device same-frame chord (a mouse-only chord can't have drag.active — the left-press edge implies a prior release that clears the drag), so NOT a mouse-parity blocker — but the executor-ordering inconsistency is real and defeats the deliberate drag-interrupt latch.
findings.recommended_fix: Emit Press_Anchor only when a same-frame Cancel was actually emitted (the placing-chord case), or order it before Right_Click.

findings.title: drive_parity re-applies the already-fast-path-applied action log through pp.step — the parity goldens pin a double-applied state no real path produces
findings.location: harness/parity.odin:163-170 (batch from action_log at apply_tick) vs app/main.odin:303 (pp.step with {} — 'edits land via the fast-path') + core/topology.odin:158-174 (validate_draw has no duplicate-pipe rejection), 176-197 (apply_draw appends unconditionally)
findings.evidence: commit_draw applies Draw{0,1} at map/exec time AND logs it at apply_tick=1; the tick loop then feeds the log back through pp.step, whose step.odin:61 topology_apply_edit re-applies it — validate_draw passes (no dup check) and apply_draw appends a SECOND parallel pipe. The draw scenario's blessed golden hashes therefore describe two parallel pipes where the app/replay have one.
findings.detail: Cross-device equality still holds (all devices double-apply identically), so the parity purpose is served — but the blessed T1 manifests pin a fantasy state, diverging from the app (empty-batch step) and from replay (single application). A future single-apply fix changes the goldens (deliberate re-bless).
findings.recommended_fix: Step with an empty batch in drive_parity (pp.step(&state, sim_tick, {}, cat)) mirroring app/main.odin:303, then re-bless the two input_parity manifests.

findings.recommended_fix: Change && to || (fail when either field became selected).

findings.evidence: Odin zero-initializes the omitted i64 to 0; drive_parity assigns ictx.sel_pipe = sel_pipe (0 = a REAL preset; -1 = none everywhere else). All 15 sibling no-preset scenarios write sel_pipe = -1 explicitly.
findings.detail: X demolishes pipe 0 via the preset even if the click-select frames are dropped or click_select regresses — the scenario's middle step can never fail.
findings.recommended_fix: Add sel_pipe = -1 to the literal; fix the struct comment to '-1 = none selected'.
